# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤲]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤲]

I can see a yellow light, display reading 0, and five wires in order: white, green, yellow, blue, red. The manual-holder needs these observations to identify the correct procedure and instruct the Blind, who alone can act. The incoming 🤲 gestures do not yet have an established meaning.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I see display 0, yellow light, and wires in order 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. Please use the manual to determine the required action and tell Blind.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The bomb remains unchanged. I received a ✌ gesture from Mute, but no meaning has been established for that sign, so I should not infer an instruction from it. I will ensure Blind has the visual layout and ask Mute to communicate the manual’s exact procedure in speech, which both Mute and Blind can hear.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="I see display 0, yellow light, and wires in order 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. Mute has the manual; wait for the exact procedure.")
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the manual's exact instruction to Blind, including which control or wire to use and any required order. The ✌ gesture has no established meaning yet.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The board is still unchanged, and I have received no new information. The earlier ✌ gesture remains uninterpreted; it cannot safely substitute for the manual’s instruction. I should again prompt Mute to speak the exact procedure directly to Blind, while keeping Blind aware of the unchanged visual state.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="No action has occurred and the board is unchanged. Please now speak the manual's exact procedure directly to Blind, including the required wire or control and any order.")
speak(to="blind", text="The board remains display 0, yellow light, wires 1 white 2 green 3 yellow 4 blue 5 red. I have no new instruction from Mute yet.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The bomb remains unchanged, and there is still no confirmed manual instruction. Since I cannot hear Blind or Mute, the reliable route is for Mute to speak the manual’s instruction directly to Blind; Blind should not manipulate anything until that instruction is explicit.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The board is unchanged. Please read the manual and speak its exact instruction directly to Blind now. Do not rely on gestures.")
speak(to="blind", text="No safe instruction has been received. Do not act yet; wait for Mute to state the manual's exact procedure.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The bomb is still unchanged. The previous gestures cannot safely be interpreted because no code had been assigned to them. I will now establish an explicit code with Mute: the first gesture identifies the operation, and the second identifies the wire. Mute can then signal me, and I can speak the decoded instruction to Blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The earlier gestures were unassigned. From now on, use 🤛 to mean cut, and use wire numbers as ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖐=4, 🖖=5. Send exactly two gestures: operation first, then wire number, according to the manual.")
speak(to="blind", text="I am establishing a gesture code with Mute. Do not act yet. Mute will signal me with the manual's operation and wire number, and I will state the decoded instruction aloud.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤛 ✌]

Mute’s two gestures match the code I established: 🤛 means cut, and ✌ means wire 2. Therefore the manual’s instruction is to cut the second wire, which is green. I will relay that exact action to Blind.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The instruction is: cut wire 2, the green wire.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[white]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The cut was correct, and the bomb has advanced to a new state: the light is now blue, display remains 0, and the remaining wires are 1 yellow, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 white. I should pass this new visual state to Mute so the manual can determine the next operation, and tell Blind not to act until Mute’s instruction is decoded.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Correct cut. New state: light blue, display 0. Remaining wires: 1 yellow, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 white; wire 2 is cut. Use the manual to determine the next instruction and signal it with the established code.")
speak(to="blind", text="The cut was correct and the bomb changed. New visual state: blue light, display 0; wire 2 is cut; remaining wires are 1 yellow, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 white. Wait for the next instruction.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[white]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤛 🖖]

Mute’s gestures match the established code: 🤛 means cut and 🖖 means wire 5. The next action is therefore to cut wire 5, the white wire. I will relay that instruction to Blind.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The next instruction is: cut wire 5, the white wire.")
```
